metadata.title: Hosting Model Trust

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for establishing explicit trust assumptions based on where computing platforms are physically hosted and operationally managed.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Physical hosting environments including institutional data centers, co-location facilities, third-party managed hosting, and sovereign cloud regions.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Defines environmental, jurisdictional, and operational trust assumptions for infrastructure hosting models.

metadata.remarks: Hosting Model Trust defines the trust assumptions derived from the physical location, ownership, and operational control of infrastructure hosting environments. This pattern does not prescribe physical or environmental controls; instead, it makes hosting context explicit so that higher‑level platform and system trust decisions are made knowingly.

components.title: Hosting Environment Classification
components.description: Identification and categorization of hosting environments based on ownership, operation, and jurisdiction.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid accounts associated with hosting providers or facility operations.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit classification of hosting environments to support appropriate trust assumptions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Inventory and classification of system components including hosting environments.
Security architecture reflects hosting model assumptions.

components.title: Operational Control Boundaries
components.description: Clear definition of operational responsibility boundaries between institution, provider, and third parties.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Exploitation of externally exposed management or hosting service interfaces.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit assignment and governance of operational responsibilities.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Defined roles and responsibilities for system operation.
External service and hosting dependencies are governed.
